title: The transformative power of classical music
speaker: Benjamin Zander

sentences.en: Probably a lot of you know the story of the two salesmen who went down to Africa in the 1900s.
sentences.zh: 相信很多人都听过两个推销员的故事，他们在20世纪去往非洲

sentences.en: They were sent down to find if there was any opportunity for selling shoes, and they wrote telegrams back to Manchester.
sentences.zh: 调研当地是否有卖鞋的商机。不久，电报就派回了曼切斯特

sentences.en: And one of them wrote, "Situation hopeless. Stop. They don't wear shoes."
sentences.zh: 其中一人写道：“情况堪忧，中止计划。非洲人不穿鞋。”

sentences.en: And the other one wrote, "Glorious opportunity. They don't have any shoes yet."
sentences.zh: 另一个人写道：“天赐良机！他们都还没有鞋呢！”（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, there's a similar situation in the classical music world, because there are some people who think that classical music is dying.
sentences.zh: 其实，古典音乐的殿堂正面临相同的处境。有人觉得古典音乐正在消亡。

sentences.en: And there are some of us who think you ain't seen nothing yet.
sentences.zh: 而另一群人觉得这不过是刚刚开始。

sentences.en: And rather than go into statistics and trends, and tell you about all the orchestras that are closing, and the record companies that are folding, I thought we should do an experiment tonight.
sentences.zh: 我不准备给你们看什么统计数据和趋势，也不打算说那些业已解散的管弦乐队的故事、或歇业的唱片公司。今晚，我想做个实验， 一个实验。

sentences.en: Actually, it's not really an experiment, because I know the outcome.
sentences.zh: 其实我已经知道结果，所以这并不算是个实验。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But it's like an experiment. Now, before we start -- (Laughter) Before we start, I need to do two things.
sentences.zh: 但它毕竟是个实验。好，在--（笑声）--在开始前，我想先做两件事。

sentences.en: One is I want to remind you of what a seven-year-old child sounds like when he plays the piano.
sentences.zh: 第一，我想你想象一下，一个7岁的小孩子弹出的琴声。

sentences.en: Maybe you have this child at home. He sounds something like this.
sentences.zh: 你家里可能就有这么一个小孩。他听起来像这样。

sentences.en: (Music) (Music ends)
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）

sentences.en: I see some of you recognize this child. Now, if he practices for a year and takes lessons, he's now eight and he sounds like this.
sentences.zh: 我知道有些人认识这个小孩。好，如果他练习一年，上些课，他八岁了，他听起来像这样。（钢琴声）

sentences.en: (Music) (Music ends) He practices for another year and takes lessons -- he's nine.
sentences.zh: (音乐结束) 他再练习一年 并学习——他才九岁。

sentences.en: (Music) (Music ends) Then he practices for another year and takes lessons -- now he's 10.
sentences.zh: 他再练上一年，上些课；现在他九岁了。

sentences.en: (Music) (Music ends) At that point, they usually give up.
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）然后他再练习，上课，他十岁了。（钢琴声）这时候他们一般就放弃了。（笑声）（掌声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) Now, if you'd waited for one more year, you would have heard this.
sentences.zh: 其实，如果你在等等，再等上一年，你会听到这个：

sentences.en: (Music) (Music ends) Now, what happened was not maybe what you thought,
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）其实，发生的情况和人想像的并不一样，

sentences.en: which is, he suddenly became passionate, engaged, involved, got a new teacher, he hit puberty, or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 那个孩子并没有突然变得很热爱，投入，找了新老师，或者突然开窍。

sentences.en: What actually happened was the impulses were reduced.
sentences.zh: 其实是当中的停顿减少了。

sentences.en: You see, the first time, he was playing with an impulse on every note.
sentences.zh: 看，第一次他弹的时候每弹一个音符就要停顿一次。（钢琴声）

sentences.en: (Music) And the second, with an impulse every other note.
sentences.zh: 现在是两个音符停顿一次。（钢琴声）

sentences.en: (Music) You can see it by looking at my head.
sentences.zh: 看我的头你就能看出来。（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) The nine-year-old put an impulse on every four notes.
sentences.zh: 现在是9岁的小孩，9岁4个音符。（钢琴声）

sentences.en: (Music) The 10-year-old, on every eight notes.
sentences.zh: 十岁的时候，8个。（钢琴声）。

sentences.en: (Music) And the 11-year-old, one impulse on the whole phrase.
sentences.zh: 到了11岁，整个段落只有一处停顿。（钢琴声）

sentences.en: (Music) I don't know how we got into this position.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我的姿势怎么突然成了这样，（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) I didn't say, "I'm going to move my shoulder over, move my body."
sentences.zh: 我脑子里没有想过要把肩膀移到这里，身体移到那里。

sentences.en: No, the music pushed me over, which is why I call it one-buttock playing.
sentences.zh: 没有，是音乐在推动我，我管这叫做半个屁股的演奏。（钢琴声）也可能是另外半个屁股。

sentences.en: (Music) It can be the other buttock. (Music) You know, a gentleman was once watching a presentation I was doing, when I was working with a young pianist.
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）一位男士曾经观看我与一个青年钢琴家合作。

sentences.en: He was the president of a corporation in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 他是俄亥俄州一间公司的老板。我和那个青年钢琴家说，

sentences.en: I was working with this young pianist, and said, "The trouble with you is you're a two-buttock player.
sentences.zh: “你的问题在于，你只会‘整个屁股的演奏’。你应该坐半个屁股来演奏。”

sentences.en: You should be a one-buttock player." I moved his body while he was playing.
sentences.zh: 当他演奏的时候我就这样移动了他的身体。

sentences.en: And suddenly, the music took off. It took flight.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间音乐就像乘着翅膀飞了起来。

sentences.en: The audience gasped when they heard the difference.
sentences.zh: 观众听到这个改变都吃了一大惊。

sentences.en: Then I got a letter from this gentleman.
sentences.zh: 后来我收到了这个公司老板的一封信。他说，“我当时感触很深，

sentences.en: He said, "I was so moved. I went back and I transformed my entire company into a one-buttock company."
sentences.zh: 于是我回去后，把我整间公司都变成了‘半个屁股公司’。”（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, the other thing I wanted to do is to tell you about you.
sentences.zh: 好，另外一件我想告诉你们的事是，

sentences.en: There are 1,600 people, I believe. My estimation is that probably 45 of you are absolutely passionate about classical music.
sentences.zh: 这里大概有1600人。我猜其中大概有45个人左右是深深热爱古典音乐的。

sentences.en: You adore classical music. Your FM is always on that classical dial.
sentences.zh: 你痴迷于古典音乐。收音机永远都调在古典音乐的频道上。

sentences.en: You have CDs in your car, and you go to the symphony, your children are playing instruments.
sentences.zh: 车里放的是古典音乐的CD, 听交响音乐会。孩子们也会弹些乐器。

sentences.en: You can't imagine your life without classical music.
sentences.zh: 你不能想象没有古典音乐的生活是怎么样的。

sentences.en: That's the first group, quite small. Then there's another bigger group.
sentences.zh: 这是第一种人，为数不多。另一种人，大多数的，

sentences.en: The people who don't mind classical music.
sentences.zh: 是不讨厌古典音乐的人。（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) You know, you've come home from a long day, and you take a glass of wine, and you put your feet up.
sentences.zh: 你结束了一天的辛苦工作回到家里，为自己倒了杯红酒，坐下把脚翘起来。

sentences.en: A little Vivaldi in the background doesn't do any harm.
sentences.zh: 来一点威尔第的音乐。真好。（笑声）

sentences.en: That's the second group. Now comes the third group: people who never listen to classical music.
sentences.zh: 这是第二种人。第三种人，他们从不接触古典音乐。

sentences.en: It's just simply not part of your life. You might hear it like second-hand smoke at the airport ...
sentences.zh: 古典音乐根本就不是他们生活的一部分。你听它，就像在机场里吸二手烟一样稀松平常。

sentences.en: (Laughter) -- and maybe a little bit of a march from "Aida" when you come into the hall.
sentences.zh: （笑声）或者当你走进某大楼时，耳边刮到一点《阿依达》的进行曲除此之外与古典乐再没有交集。

sentences.en: But otherwise, you never hear it. That's probably the largest group.
sentences.zh: 这大概就是为数最多的一群人。

sentences.en: And then there's a very small group. These are the people who think they're tone-deaf.
sentences.zh: 最后，还有为数不多的一群人。这些人认为自己是音盲。真神奇，很多人都认为自己是音盲。

sentences.en: Amazing number of people think they're tone-deaf.
sentences.zh: 令人吃惊的人 认为他们是音盲。

sentences.en: Actually, I hear a lot, "My husband is tone-deaf."
sentences.zh: 事实上我听到过很多，“我老公是个音盲。”（笑声)

sentences.en: (Laughter) Actually, you cannot be tone-deaf.
sentences.zh: 你不可能是音盲。没有人是音盲。

sentences.en: Nobody is tone-deaf. If you were tone-deaf, you couldn't change the gears on your car, in a stick shift car.
sentences.zh: 如果你音盲，你根本无法给汽车换档，如果你开的是手档车话。

sentences.en: You couldn't tell the difference between somebody from Texas and somebody from Rome.
sentences.zh: 你听不出来德克萨斯州和罗马来的两个人讲话有什么区别。

sentences.en: And the telephone. The telephone. If your mother calls on the miserable telephone, she calls and says, "Hello," you not only know who it is, you know what mood she's in.
sentences.zh: 还有电话。如果你妈妈打电话给你，她用悲伤的语调说，“你好，”你不仅知道她是谁，还知道她心情的好坏。

sentences.en: You have a fantastic ear. Everybody has a fantastic ear.
sentences.zh: 你有双神奇的耳朵。每个人都有双神奇的耳朵。所以没有人是音盲。

sentences.en: So nobody is tone-deaf. But I tell you what.
sentences.zh: 所以没人是音盲 但我告诉你

sentences.en: It doesn't work for me to go on with this thing, with such a wide gulf between those who understand, love and are passionate about classical music, and those who have no relationship to it at all.
sentences.zh: 但是，让我来告诉你，如果我要继续我的事业，这些种种将对我不起作用人们对古典音乐的认知存在巨大差异。有人痴迷，有人无视。

sentences.en: The tone-deaf people, they're no longer here.
sentences.zh: 即便“音盲”是不存在的，

sentences.en: But even between those three categories, it's too wide a gulf.
sentences.zh: 但是剩下三组人的差距还是很大。

sentences.en: So I'm not going to go on until every single person in this room, downstairs and in Aspen, and everybody else looking, will come to love and understand classical music.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不会继续下去，直到这屋子里的每个人，楼上楼下，每个人都来试图理解和热爱古典音乐。

sentences.en: So that's what we're going to do. Now, you notice that there is not the slightest doubt in my mind that this is going to work, if you look at my face, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天要做的事情。你有没有发现，我对我的想法没有一丝的怀疑。你看我的脸，就知道我认为这一定能成功，是不是？

sentences.en: It's one of the characteristics of a leader that he not doubt for one moment the capacity of the people he's leading to realize whatever he's dreaming.
sentences.zh: 这是一个坚定不移的领导者的特质，他让他所领导的人民深信他的能力，逐步实现梦想。

sentences.en: Imagine if Martin Luther King had said, "I have a dream.
sentences.zh: 想想看，如果马丁路德金说，“我有一个梦想！但是，我不确定你们是不是乐意追跟我。”

sentences.en: Of course, I'm not sure they'll be up to it."
sentences.zh: （笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) All right. So I'm going to take a piece of Chopin.
sentences.zh: 好，我要弹一首肖邦。

sentences.en: This is a beautiful prelude by Chopin. Some of you will know it.
sentences.zh: 这是一首优美的序曲。有人应该听过。

sentences.en: (Music) Do you know what I think probably happened here?
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）你猜我觉得刚刚屋里发生了什么？

sentences.en: When I started, you thought, "How beautiful that sounds."
sentences.zh: 我开始的时候，你脑子里在想,"多优美的曲子啊。“

sentences.en: (Music) "I don't think we should go to the same place
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）"明年夏天再也不要去同一个地方度假了。“

sentences.en: for our summer holidays next year." (Laughter) It's funny, isn't it?
sentences.zh: （笑声）有趣吧？这些想法

sentences.en: It's funny how those thoughts kind of waft into your head.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的就飘到你脑海中去了。

sentences.en: And of course -- (Applause) Of course, if the piece is long and you've had a long day, you might actually drift off.
sentences.zh: （掌声）当然，如果这首曲子很长，而且你很累，你可能会不知不觉睡着了。

sentences.en: Then your companion will dig you in the ribs and say, "Wake up! It's culture!" And then you feel even worse.
sentences.zh: 你旁边的同伴就会戳戳你，说，”醒醒！这是文化！“你会感到更郁闷。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But has it ever occurred to you that the reason you feel sleepy in classical music is not because of you, but because of us?
sentences.zh: 但是你有没有想过，你之所以在听古典音乐的时候会觉得困，不是因为你，而是因为我们？在我演奏的时候，有没有人想：

sentences.en: Did anybody think while I was playing, "Why is he using so many impulses?"
sentences.zh: “为什么他用了这么多的停顿？”

sentences.en: If I'd done this with my head you certainly would have thought it.
sentences.zh: 如果我动了我的脑袋的话，你肯定想的到。

sentences.en: (Music) (Music ends) And for the rest of your life, every time you hear classical music, you'll always be able to know if you hear those impulses.
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）在你未来的人生中，每当你听到古典音乐你都会意识到自己是否听到了这些停顿。好，让我们来看看这到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: So let's see what's really going on here.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看这里到底发生了什么

sentences.en: We have a B. This is a B. The next note is a C.
sentences.zh: 这是个B, 它旁边的这个是C.

sentences.en: And the job of the C is to make the B sad.
sentences.zh: C的任务就是让B听起来很哀伤。它做到了，是不是？

sentences.en: And it does, doesn't it? (Laughter) Composers know that.
sentences.zh: （笑声）作曲家知道这个秘诀，所以如果他们想要创作悲伤的音乐，

sentences.en: If they want sad music, they just play those two notes.
sentences.zh: 他们就不停的用这两个音符。（钢琴声）

sentences.en: (Music) But basically, it's just a B, with four sads.
sentences.zh: 其实就是一个B,和4个悲伤而已。（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, it goes down to A. Now to G.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们下降到A,到G,最后到F。

sentences.en: And then to F. So we have B, A, G, F. And if we have B, A, G, F, what do we expect next?
sentences.zh: 好，我们有，B A G F，如果我们有 B A G F，接下来你将期待什么？ 哦，好像事有凑巧。

sentences.en: (Music) That might have been a fluke. Let's try it again.
sentences.zh: 这可能是个意外 我们再试一次

sentences.en: (Music) Oh, the TED choir. (Laughter) And you notice nobody is tone-deaf, right?
sentences.zh: 再试一次。 哈， TED合唱团。（笑声）你有没有发现，没有人是音盲，对不对？没有人。

sentences.en: Nobody is. You know, every village in Bangladesh and every hamlet in China -- everybody knows: da, da -- da.
sentences.zh: 每一个孟加拉国的小镇，每一个中国的村庄，每个人，都知道：嗒，嗒，嗒，嗒 - 嗒。每个人都知道下一个是E。

sentences.en: Everybody knows, who's expecting that E.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道,谁在等待E。

sentences.en: Chopin didn't want to reach the E there, because what will have happened?
sentences.zh: 不过，Chopin还不想到E。不然会怎么样？ 曲子就结束了，就像《哈姆雷特》。

sentences.en: It will be over, like Hamlet. Do you remember?
sentences.zh: 记不记得《哈姆雷特》？第一幕，第三场：

sentences.en: Act One, scene three, he finds out his uncle killed his father.
sentences.zh: 他发现他的叔叔杀了他的父亲。你记不记得他靠近他的叔叔

sentences.en: He keeps on going up to his uncle and almost killing him.
sentences.zh: 差点杀了他。但是他又走开了。

sentences.en: And then he backs away, he goes up to him again, almost kills him.
sentences.zh: 他又靠过去，差点杀了他。所有的评论家都坐在后排那里，

sentences.en: The critics sitting in the back row there, they have to have an opinion, so they say, "Hamlet is a procrastinator."
sentences.zh: 他们必须要批评点什么，于是他们说，“哈姆雷特优柔寡断，拖泥带水。”（笑声）或者，“哈姆雷特有恋母情结。”

sentences.en: Or they say, "Hamlet has an Oedipus complex."
sentences.zh: 或者他们说,"哈姆雷特有一个俄狄浦斯综合体。"

sentences.en: No, otherwise the play would be over, stupid.
sentences.zh: 不是的，不然这演出就结束了，傻瓜。

sentences.en: (Laughter) That's why Shakespeare puts all that stuff in Hamlet -- Ophelia going mad, the play within the play, and Yorick's skull, and the gravediggers.
sentences.zh: 所以莎士比亚才把这些东西放进去。Ophelia在戏中发疯，Yorick的头盖骨，还有盗墓人。

sentences.en: That's in order to delay -- until Act Five, he can kill him.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了推迟——直到在第五幕他杀掉他叔叔。

sentences.en: It's the same with the Chopin. He's just about to reach the E, and he says, "Oops, better go back up and do it again."
sentences.zh: Chopin也是一样的。他马上就要到E了，他说，“不行，反复一遍会更好。”

sentences.en: So he does it again. Now, he gets excited.
sentences.zh: 于是他又来一遍。这里他变的很激昂，这部分

sentences.en: (Music) That's excitement, don't worry about it.
sentences.zh: 你不用管。

sentences.en: Now, he gets to F-sharp, and finally he goes down to E, but it's the wrong chord -- because the chord he's looking for is this one, and instead he does ...
sentences.zh: 这他到了升半音的的F, 终于到了E。但是这是不对的和铉。他想要的和铉是这个，但是他用了。

sentences.en: Now, we call that a deceptive cadence, because it deceives us.
sentences.zh: 我们管这个叫假旋律，因为它是为了欺骗我们用的。我总是告诉学生，“如果你要弹到假旋律，

sentences.en: I tell my students, "If you have a deceptive cadence, raise your eyebrows, and everybody will know."
sentences.zh: 把你的眉毛抬起来大家就知道了。”（笑声）（掌声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) Right. He gets to E, but it's the wrong chord.
sentences.zh: 好，他到了E，但是是错的和铉。他再次试E， 这个和铉也不好。

sentences.en: Now, he tries E again. That chord doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 现在，他再次尝试E。那个和弦不行。

sentences.en: Now, he tries the E again. That chord doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 他再试，这个也不行。

sentences.en: Now, he tries E again, and that doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 他再试，还是不行。

sentences.en: And then finally ... There was a gentleman in the front row who went, "Mmm."
sentences.zh: 终于。。坐在第一排的这位男士刚刚，“啊。。”放松了。

sentences.en: (Laughter) It's the same gesture he makes when he comes home after a long day, turns off the key in his car and says, "Aah, I'm home."
sentences.zh: 这与他回到家的时候做的是同样的姿势。经过一天辛苦的工作，他拧钥匙熄灭了他的车，说，“啊，我到家了。”因为我们都知道家是哪。

sentences.en: Because we all know where home is. So this is a piece which goes from away to home.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是从远方回家的曲子。我这就来把它从头到尾的演奏一遍。

sentences.en: I'm going to play it all the way through and you're going to follow.
sentences.zh: 你会跟随这琴声，B, C, B, C, B, C, B--

sentences.en: B, C, B, C, B, C, B -- down to A, down to G, down to F.
sentences.zh: 到A，到G，到F

sentences.en: Almost goes to E, but otherwise the play would be over.
sentences.zh: 马上就要到E了，可是曲子那样会结束。

sentences.en: He goes back up to B, he gets very excited.
sentences.zh: 于是他回到B，这里变的很激动，到F声调，到E。

sentences.en: Goes to F-sharp. Goes to E. It's the wrong chord. It's the wrong chord.
sentences.zh: 可是是错的和铉，错的和铉，错的和铉。

sentences.en: And finally goes to E, and it's home. And what you're going to see is one-buttock playing.
sentences.zh: 终于它弹到了E，那里是家。而且你马上要看到的是“半个屁股演奏法”。（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Because for me, to join the B to the E, I have to stop thinking about every single note along the way, and start thinking about the long, long line from B to E.
sentences.zh: 因为，如果我想要把B和E链接起来的话，我要停止去想中间的每一个音符，而是开始想这从B到E流下来的一条线。

sentences.en: You know, we were just in South Africa, and you can't go to South Africa without thinking of Mandela in jail for 27 years.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚说到南非，如果你不去想曼德拉在铁窗中的27年，你是不能理解南非的。

sentences.en: What was he thinking about? Lunch? No, he was thinking about the vision for South Africa and for human beings.
sentences.zh: 他当时在想些什么？午饭么？不是，他在想南非的将来，人类的将来。

sentences.en: This is about vision. This is about the long line.
sentences.zh: 这是关于将来的一曲，关于这条长长的线。

sentences.en: Like the bird who flies over the field and doesn't care about the fences underneath, all right?
sentences.zh: 就好象鸟儿从天空中飞过田地，不会去管地上的栅栏一样，不是吗？

sentences.en: So now, you're going to follow the line all the way from B to E.
sentences.zh: 所以，请你跟随我从B到E，连成一线。

sentences.en: And I've one last request before I play this piece all the way through.
sentences.zh: 在我开始演奏之前，我还有一个请求。

sentences.en: Would you think of somebody who you adore, who's no longer there?
sentences.zh: 请你想起一个你爱的人，但是他/她已经不在了。

sentences.en: A beloved grandmother, a lover -- somebody in your life who you love with all your heart, but that person is no longer with you.
sentences.zh: 比如关爱你的奶奶，或者以前的爱人。一个在你生命中，让你用尽全心去爱的人，但是他/她已经不在了。

sentences.en: Bring that person into your mind, and at the same time, follow the line all the way from B to E, and you'll hear everything that Chopin had to say.
sentences.zh: 把他/她放在你的脑海中，同时，跟随着我，从B到E。你会听到一切肖邦想说的话语。

sentences.en: (Music) (Music ends)
sentences.zh: （钢琴声）

sentences.en: (Applause) Now, you may be wondering -- (Applause)
sentences.zh: （掌声）你可能在想，

sentences.en: (Applause ends) You may be wondering why I'm clapping.
sentences.zh: 你可能在想为什么我在鼓掌。

sentences.en: Well, I did this at a school in Boston with about 70 seventh graders, 12-year-olds.
sentences.zh: 因为，我在波士顿作这个演奏受众是七十个7年纪的学生们，12岁。

sentences.en: I did exactly what I did with you, and I explained the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我做了同样的事情，我告诉他们，给他们解释了一切。

sentences.en: At the end, they went crazy, clapping. I was clapping. They were clapping.
sentences.zh: 曲子结束的时候，他们都狂呼了起来，鼓掌。他们在鼓掌，我也在鼓掌。他们在鼓掌。

sentences.en: Finally, I said, "Why am I clapping?" And one of them said, "Because we were listening."
sentences.zh: 我问，“为什么我也在鼓掌？”一个小孩叫到，“因为我们在听。”（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Think of it. 1,600 people, busy people, involved in all sorts of different things, listening, understanding and being moved
sentences.zh: 想象一下。1600个人，忙碌的人。每个人都有这不同的职业。每个人都认真聆听，理解，而且被这首肖邦感动。

sentences.en: by a piece by Chopin. Now, that is something.
sentences.zh: 这也算是成功了吧。

sentences.en: Am I sure that every single person followed that, understood it, was moved by it?
sentences.zh: 我是不是能确定屋子里的每一个人都跟随着理解了，而且被感动了呢？我不确定。

sentences.en: Of course, I can't be sure. But I'll tell you what happened to me in Ireland during the Troubles, 10 years ago, and I was working with some Catholic and Protestant kids on conflict resolution.
sentences.zh: 但是我要给你讲一个故事。10年前的爱尔兰正值动乱，我正好在那里。我去那里帮助一些天主教徒和新基督教徒的孩子解决一些矛盾问题。我也表演了刚才那一段。

sentences.en: And I did this with them -- a risky thing to do, because they were street kids.
sentences.zh: 这是一件冒险的事。因为他们都是些在街头流浪的孩子。

sentences.en: And one of them came to me the next morning and he said, "You know, I've never listened to classical music in my life, but when you played that shopping piece ..."
sentences.zh: 可第二天早晨，其中一个小孩找到我，他说，“我从来没有听过古典音乐，但是你弹的那个‘购物单’……“（肖邦在英文中音近购物）（笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) He said, "My brother was shot last year and I didn't cry for him.
sentences.zh: 他说，”我的哥哥去年被枪杀了，我没有为他掉一滴眼泪。

sentences.en: But last night, when you played that piece, he was the one I was thinking about.
sentences.zh: 但是昨晚你弹到那曲的时候，我在想我的哥哥。

sentences.en: And I felt the tears streaming down my face.
sentences.zh: 我感到了自己的眼泪顺着脸颊淌下来。

sentences.en: And it felt really good to cry for my brother."
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，为哥哥哭的这种感觉很好。“

sentences.en: So I made up my mind at that moment that classical music is for everybody.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻起，我就坚信，古典音乐可以打动每一个人，每一个人。

sentences.en: Everybody. Now, how would you walk -- my profession, the music profession doesn't see it that way.
sentences.zh: 你怎么走路？你知道，我的行业，音乐行业不这么想。

sentences.en: They say three percent of the population likes classical music.
sentences.zh: 他们说，3%的人喜欢古典音乐。

sentences.en: If only we could move it to four percent, our problems would be over.
sentences.zh: 如果要是有4%，我们的世界就不会有那么多的问题了。

sentences.en: (Laughter) How would you walk? How would you talk? How would you be?
sentences.zh: 我说，”你怎么走路？怎么说话？如果你只认为

sentences.en: If you thought, "Three percent of the population likes classical music, if only we could move it to four percent."
sentences.zh: 3%的人喜欢古典音乐,如果有4%就好了，你怎么走路？

sentences.en: How would you walk or talk? How would you be?
sentences.zh: 怎么说话？如果你知道

sentences.en: If you thought, "Everybody loves classical music -- they just haven't found out about it yet."
sentences.zh: 每一个人都热爱古典音乐，只是他们不知道罢了。“（笑声）

sentences.en: See, these are totally different worlds.
sentences.zh: 看，这将是一个大不同的世界。

sentences.en: Now, I had an amazing experience. I was 45 years old, I'd been conducting for 20 years, and I suddenly had a realization.
sentences.zh: 我45岁的时候有个特别的经历。我在我指挥乐队20年以后，突然有一天意识到，

sentences.en: The conductor of an orchestra doesn't make a sound.
sentences.zh: 乐团指挥自己完全不出一声。

sentences.en: My picture appears on the front of the CD -- (Laughter) But the conductor doesn't make a sound.
sentences.zh: 我的照片会跑到CD的封面上去--（笑声）但是其实指挥一声也不出。

sentences.en: He depends, for his power, on his ability to make other people powerful.
sentences.zh: 他的能量在于发挥别人的力量。

sentences.en: And that changed everything for me. It was totally life-changing.
sentences.zh: 这个观点改变了我的一切。那是一个对整个生活态度的改变。我的管弦乐队里的人跟我说，

sentences.en: People in my orchestra said, "Ben, what happened?" That's what happened.
sentences.zh: ”本, 怎么回事？“就是这么回事。

sentences.en: I realized my job was to awaken possibility in other people.
sentences.zh: 我意识到了，我的任务就是发觉别人的潜力。当然，我想知道我有没有做到这点。

sentences.en: And of course, I wanted to know whether I was doing that.
sentences.zh: 当然，我想知道我是否正在这样做。

sentences.en: How do you find out? You look at their eyes.
sentences.zh: 你知道我怎么发现吗？我看他们的眼睛。

sentences.en: If their eyes are shining, you know you're doing it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们的眼睛闪光,你就知道你做到了。这个小伙子的眼睛可以照亮一个小镇。

sentences.en: You could light up a village with this guy's eyes.
sentences.zh: （笑声）

sentences.en: (Laughter) Right. So if the eyes are shining, you know you're doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你看到了闪光的眼睛，你就知道你做到了。如果他们的眼睛没有闪光，你就要问一个问题。

sentences.en: If the eyes are not shining, you get to ask a question.
sentences.zh: 这样一个问题：

sentences.en: And this is the question: who am I being that my players' eyes are not shining?
sentences.zh: 如果我的队员们的眼睛没有闪光，我的存在是为了什么？

sentences.en: We can do that with our children, too. Who am I being, that my children's eyes are not shining?
sentences.zh: 这也可以用在我们的孩子身上。如果我的孩子们的眼睛没有闪光，我的存在是为了什么？

sentences.en: That's a totally different world. Now, we're all about to end this magical, on-the-mountain week, we're going back into the world.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大为不同的世界。我们马上就要结束这个神奇的，山顶上的一周了，我们马上就要回到现实世界里。

sentences.en: And I say, it's appropriate for us to ask the question, who are we being as we go back out into the world?
sentences.zh: 我想，我们应该问自己一个问题：我们回到现实世界中能做一些什么？

sentences.en: And you know, I have a definition of success.
sentences.zh: 我有一个成功的定义。

sentences.en: For me, it's very simple. It's not about wealth and fame and power.
sentences.zh: 这个定义很简单。它不是财富，名誉，权利。

sentences.en: It's about how many shining eyes I have around me.
sentences.zh: 是在我身边有多少双闪光的眼睛。

sentences.en: So now, I have one last thought, which is that it really makes a difference what we say -- the words that come out of our mouth.
sentences.zh: 我有最后一个想跟大家分享的想法，就是我们的话语造成的不同。我们嘴里说出来的话有没有造成不同。

sentences.en: I learned this from a woman who survived Auschwitz, one of the rare survivors.
sentences.zh: 我从一个在奥斯威辛集中营活下来的女士那里学到了这个。她是少数的幸存者之一。

sentences.en: She went to Auschwitz when she was 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 她在15岁的时候被关进了奥斯威辛集中营。

sentences.en: And ... And her brother was eight, and the parents were lost.
sentences.zh: 那时她的弟弟8岁，他们的父母都被杀害了。

sentences.en: And she told me this, she said, "We were in the train going to Auschwitz, and I looked down and saw my brother's shoes were missing.
sentences.zh: 她告诉了我这个，她说，“我们在去奥斯威辛的火车上，我低头的时候发现我弟弟的鞋不见了。

sentences.en: I said, 'Why are you so stupid, can't you keep your things together for goodness' sake?'"
sentences.zh: 我很生气，说，”你怎么这么笨，看在上帝的份上，你就不能看好你自己的东西吗？”——用一种大姐

sentences.en: The way an elder sister might speak to a younger brother.
sentences.zh: 会和弟弟说话的方式。不幸的是，这是她对她弟弟说的最后一句话。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, it was the last thing she ever said to him, because she never saw him again.
sentences.zh: 她再也没有见过她弟弟。他没有幸存下来。

sentences.en: He did not survive. And so when she came out of Auschwitz, she made a vow.
sentences.zh: 当她从奥斯威辛活下来后，她发了个誓。

sentences.en: She told me this. She said, "I walked out of Auschwitz into life and I made a vow.
sentences.zh: 她说，”我活着从奥斯威辛走了出来，

sentences.en: And the vow was, "I will never say anything that couldn't stand as the last thing I ever say."
sentences.zh: 我发了个誓。这誓言就是，我再也不会说任何一句话如果那句话不能当做我死前的最后一句。“

sentences.en: Now, can we do that? No. And we'll make ourselves wrong and others wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们能做到这点么？不能。我们都会犯错。

sentences.en: But it is a possibility to live into. Thank you.
sentences.zh: 但是这是一个我们可能去努力达到的生活态度。谢谢。

sentences.en: (Applause) Shining eyes. (Applause) Shining eyes.
sentences.zh: （掌声）

sentences.en: (Applause) Thank you, thank you.
sentences.zh: 闪光的眼睛，闪光的眼睛。
